title: Normalized scalar continuous cochains versus the internal derived bar total
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, and a finite intermediate field $E$. For $F\in\{E,\Omega\}$ put $A(S)=C(S,F)$ with all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Work on the small coherent profinite site in [def-weil-size-convention], in ordinary internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and their ordinary derived category [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group whose finite continuous quotients all have order prime to $\ell$, acting trivially on $A$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Define the nonnegative cochain complex $\mathcal C_F^\bullet(K)$ by $\mathcal C_F^n(K)(S)=C(S\times K^n,F)$, with $d^0=0$ and
$$(dc)(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=c(s;g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{a=1}^{n}(-1)^a c(s;g_1,\ldots,g_ag_{a+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}c(s;g_1,\ldots,g_n).$$
Let $A[\underline K^n]$ be the free internal $A$-module on $S\mapsto C(S,K^n)$, and let $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A$ be the right adjoint of internal module tensor. Use compatible nonnegative equivariant injective resolutions and the inhomogeneous nerve of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data] to form
$$\mathscr B_F(K)=\operatorname{Tot}_{n\geq0}R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline K^n],A[0]).$$
Here $[0]$ places a module in cochain degree zero, and the finite-diagonal resolution total has differential $d_{bar}+(-1)^n d_{res}$. Evaluation identifies $\mathcal C_F^n(K)$ with the underived internal Hom. A resolution augmentation $A\to I^\bullet$ therefore specifies maps into resolution degree zero in every bar degree. These maps commute with every nerve face, have zero composite with the next resolution differential, and give a cochain augmentation into the total. Denote its localization by
$$j_{K,F}:Q(\mathcal C_F^\bullet(K))\longrightarrow\mathscr B_F(K),$$
where $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms. The actual morphism $j_{K,F}$ is an isomorphism. It is independent of compatible resolution choices, with the comparison identifications fixed by the augmentations. If $u:A[0]\to\mathcal C_F^\bullet(K)$ is the identity in degree zero, then $j_{K,F}Q(u)$ is the resolution augmentation induced by invariant inclusion in bar degree zero. For $K=1$ this is the ordinary resolution comparison of $A[0]$. The coefficient $\Omega$ remains noncomplete. This is a comparison with a derived bar total before evaluation at a point; no assertion that the individual internal Hom columns are acyclic is included.

proof.text: Choose an equivariant injective resolution $s:A[0]\to I^\bullet$. By [lem-sfb-homogeneous-injective-total-target], its underlying resolution is injective. Use [lem-sfb-profinite-free-hom-resolution-evaluation] with $P=K^p$ to identify the bar columns with $D^{p,q}(S)=I^q(S\times K^p)$, their augmentations with $s$, and their parameter maps with pullback. In particular $\ker d_v^{p,0}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline K^p],A)=\mathcal C_F^p(K)$. The nerve faces on this kernel give exactly the displayed trivial-action differential. The maps to $(p,0)$ commute with these faces by equivariance of $s$, and $d_vs=0$. They therefore define the specified $j_{\rm chain}:\mathcal C_F^\bullet(K)\to\operatorname{Tot}D$. Its localization targets the compatible derived bar model by [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar].

proof.text: For $F=E$, apply [lem-sfb-normed-scalar-profinite-hom-acyclic] separately to every profinite $K^p$. Each canonical column augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism, and its parameter naturality gives the same faces as in step 1. Regard the source as a double complex concentrated in resolution degree zero. Both double complexes are first-quadrant, and [lem-sc-first-quadrant-total-column-comparison] makes their total map a quasi-isomorphism. This proves invertibility of the actual $j_{K,E}$. The finite-field completeness hypothesis is satisfied precisely in this branch.

proof.text: Now let $F=\Omega$ and put $V_{J,q}^p=H^q_v(D_J^{p,\bullet})$ internally. Fix $q>0$. Any section of $H^p_h(V_{K,q})$ is locally represented by a horizontal cocycle $x\in V_{K,q}^p$, since the quotient from horizontal cycles to cohomology is locally surjective. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-positive-bar-row-local-effacement] to that representative. On its finite parameter cover, restriction to some open $H_i$ becomes a horizontal boundary. Apply [lem-sfb-internal-bar-row-finite-index-transfer] to the SAME resolution restricted to $H_i$; its identity gives $[K:H_i][x]|_{S_i}=0$. The positive integer $[K:H_i]$ is invertible in $A(S_i)$ by the constant scalar $1/[K:H_i]\in\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq\Omega$. Hence the original class vanishes on this cover and is zero by the sheaf condition. Thus $H^p_h(V_{K,q})=0$ for every $p\geq0,q>0$. This uses local representatives and internal cohomology, without commuting arbitrary section evaluation with cohomology.

proof.text: Apply [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] in the abelian category of internal $A$-modules to $D$. Its first sequence has $E_1^{p,q}=V_{K,q}^p$ and $E_2^{p,q}=H^p_h(V_{K,q})$; its filtration is finite in every total degree. Step 1 identifies its bottom row with $\mathcal C_\Omega^\bullet(K)$. Step 3 makes every $E_2^{p,q}$ with $q>0$ zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-first-quadrant-row-collapse], the bottom edge maps are isomorphisms onto total cohomology. These are the maps induced by $j_{\rm chain}$: apply the functorial spectral sequence to the map from the double complex concentrated in row zero, whose $(p,0)$ component is $s$ and whose $E_1$ map on row zero is the identity under step 1. On $E_\infty$ it is the identity of the sole surviving graded piece, and the canonical inclusions of that piece into total cohomology are the same edges. Therefore $j_{\rm chain}$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $j_{K,\Omega}$ is invertible.

proof.text: For two equivariant resolutions of $A$, [lem-sfb-condensed-bar-total-naturality] supplies augmentation-preserving lifts, mutually inverse localized total maps, and independence of the lift by its total homotopy with sign $(-1)^p$ in bar degree $p$. For any such lift $f:I\to J$, $f^0s_I=s_J$, so $\operatorname{Tot}D(f)\,j_I=j_J$ on every $(p,0)$ component; all other source components vanish. Consequently the actual $j$ is independent of resolution under exactly the identifications fixed by those augmentations.

proof.text: The composite $j_{\rm chain}u$ has only its degree-zero component nonzero, namely $s^0:A\to I^0$ in bidegree $(0,0)$. It equals the resolution augmentation from invariant inclusion, since $A^K=A$ and its action is trivial; the normalization in [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar] is precisely this inclusion. For $K=1$, the scalar bar complex has $A$ in every nonnegative degree, differential zero in even degree and identity in odd degree. Projection to degree zero and inclusion are inverse up to the homotopy $h^n=1$ for even $n\geq2$, $h^n=0$ otherwise: directly $dh+hd=1-up$. Apply the same horizontal contraction to each resolution row (it commutes with $d_v$); the vertical cross terms cancel by the total sign. Both bar totals reduce to the respective ordinary complexes, and $j$ becomes $s:A[0]\to I^\bullet$. Thus its trivial-group normalization is the ordinary resolution comparison. Empty test sets give zero section groups throughout.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q62-fdb5ae3d8 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes, every cited statement, AGENTS.md, stages/1-dag.md, brief-stage1.md, delivery-errors A-F and paragraph (3) of the latest direct-images proof. Live still has the item unsplit with no repair note. The statement, stmt_deps and blueprint are byte-equal to live, proof_deps equals the union of uses, and nothing cites SGA. Step 1: left exactness gives ker d_v^{p,0}=C(S×K^p,F), the trivial-action first face gives the displayed differential, and d_v s=0 gives a chain map. Step 2: normed-scalar-profinite-hom-acyclic is used only for finite E, and the first-quadrant total-column comparison applies. Step 3: I recomputed [K:H]x=d_h(ty−hx) from the transfer homotopy; 1/[K:H] lies in Q⊂Ω, then sections lift locally and the sheaf condition gives zero. Step 4: the spectral sequence of Stacks 012X/0132 plus row collapse gives the edge isomorphism, and the edge is identified with j_chain. Step 5: the naturality lifts give f^0 s_I=s_J. Step 6: for K=1 the differential is 0 in even and 1 in odd degrees, h^{2k}=1 gives dh+hd=1−up, and the vertical cross terms cancel. Effacement node: true for p=0, for finite G and for the p=1 case (equivalent to E2^{1,q}=0, which follows from the item plus prime-to-ell cochain vanishing). It is not equivalent to the item, only sufficient for it, so this is not D1. It carries the open Ω analytic core under an honest WANTED and is the internal analogue of Q69's evaluated node. I could neither prove nor refute it. Transfer node: true by a finite-coset construction (internal, natural, commutes with d_v). It is not a duplicate of the continuous-cochain or averaging transfers, which need topological coefficients, and it generalizes the Q69 evaluated transfer. Batch-5: all 4 flags reach sec-trace-formula only through the generic lem-trf-free-module-sheaf-universal-property, so all are accepted. Accepted tool_uses: total-column-comparison, double-complex spectral sequences, row collapse.
